intent: Group several related fields under one shared title as a native fieldset.
typical_uses: A titled section of a form (an address, a set of notification settings)
The group of options a set of checkboxes or a RadioGroup offers, titled by a FieldLegend

dont_use_when.situation: Stacking fields with no shared title and no shared meaning
One question per step of a multi-step form
A bordered panel that frames content visually

mounted_in.container: the consuming application's own form or section element
mounted_in.note: A FieldSet may stand directly in a form; a FieldGroup around it is optional.

invariants.text: FieldSet renders a native fieldset with the user agent's border, padding, margin and min-width removed, laying its direct children out in a column with a --space-6 gap. It draws no border of its own.

`disabled` is the native fieldset attribute: it disables every native form control inside the fieldset except those inside its first legend. It does not set data-disabled on the Fields inside, so their captions are not dimmed by it. The kit controls rooted in a span (Checkbox, Switch, RadioGroupItem) do not read it either: their disabled state comes only from their own `disabled` prop and the primitive's own field and group contexts, so inside a disabled FieldSet they render no data-disabled or aria-disabled and keep their enabled styling. Pass `disabled` to those controls as well.

anti_patterns.dont: Title the set with a heading element or a FieldTitle
anti_patterns.do_instead: Make a FieldLegend the fieldset's first child, which gives the group its accessible name

good.title: A titled set of fields
good.code:
<FieldSet>
  <FieldLegend>Shipping address</FieldLegend>
  <FieldDescription>Where the order is delivered.</FieldDescription>
  <FieldGroup>
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="street">Street</FieldLabel>
      <Input id="street" />
    </Field>
  </FieldGroup>
</FieldSet>

bad.title: A set titled by a label instead of a legend
bad.why: A label names one control, not the fieldset; only a legend as the fieldset's first child names the group. Use FieldLegend, with `variant="label"` when it should read as a plain label.
